title: ESPN Unlimited Now Available on YouTube TV
description: ESPN Unlimited content is now available directly on YouTube TV, giving the streaming service’s subscribers access to thousands of additional live sp
body:
ESPN Unlimited content is now available directly on YouTube TV, giving the streaming service’s subscribers access to thousands of additional live sporting events.

	YouTube TV’s addition of ESPN Unlimited comes under the deal struck between Google and Disney reached in November 2025, after a two-week blackout of Disney-owned networks on YouTube TV. Other pay-TV providers offer customers access to ESPN Unlimited, including Disney’s Hulu + Live TV and Fubo TV, DirecTV, Charter’s Spectrum TV, Verizon FiOS, U-verse, Cox and Comcast Xfinity.
	

	The addition of ESPN Unlimited to YouTube TV comes as the Disney-owned sports giant is raising the prices of its stand-alone streaming plans: As of Sept. 17, the price of ESPN Unlimited is increasing from $29.99 to $31.99/month, with price hikes across its other plans as well.


	ESPN Unlimited, in addition to everything on the ESPN and ESPN2 linear networks, includes programming from ESPNU, ESPNews, ESPN Deportes, SECN, SECN+, ACCN, and ACCNX plus thousands of additional live sporting events per year.

	Users subscribed to the main YouTube TV plan (priced at $82.99 per month), or any plan that includes sports, can now catch all the action from ESPN such as the U.S. Open tennis, NCAA College Football, PGA Tour golf, WWE Premium Live Events, LaLiga, and out-of-market NHL games. They’ll also get access to studio shows such as “The Rich Eisen Show,” ESPN originals and films, and the complete ESPN “30 for 30” documentary library. Features like unlimited DVR, key plays, scores and stats and multiview will also be available with ESPN Unlimited content, all within the YouTube TV app.
	

	As part of the launch, YouTube TV is enhancing its menu to make it easier for viewers to find ESPN content. The live guide now shows three rows of currently airing live events from ESPN Unlimited, along with a dedicated network row for further browsing. When a game has multiple feeds, fans will now have the choice between options for different languages, home and away feeds, and alternate camera angles, all clearly labeled in our updated station picker.

	In addition, YouTube TV’s Fantasy View feature now supports ESPN Fantasy Football. ESPN Fantasy Football users can link their ESPN account through YouTube TV settings ahead of the upcoming NFL season to track their fantasy teams during live NFL games.

schema.headline: ESPN Unlimited Now Available on YouTube TV

title: Vancouver Film Festival Reveals 2026 Lineup: Jesse Eisenberg, Cristian Mungiu but Also Local Talent, Indigenous and Nonfiction Cinema
description: The 45th edition of Canada’s Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF) opens Oct. 1 with “The Debut,” Jesse Eisenberg’s offbeat comedy about comm
body:
The 45th edition of Canada’s Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF) opens Oct. 1 with “The Debut,” Jesse Eisenberg’s offbeat comedy about community theater starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti. 

	VIFF closing night film is Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine,” a black comedy set in the run-up to the 1973 Chilean coup and following CIA operatives played by John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell.




	

					‘Reclaim My Skin’
									Courtesy of VIFF
	



	One of Canada’s key film events now in the process of vigorous growth, VIFF has also unveiled its full slate of 162 features, including 12 world premieres, six international debuts, 15 North American bows and 49 Canada first screenings — alongside 91 short films and two episodic series, representing titles in all from 76 countries. 
	

	Cristian Mungiu‘s Cannes Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden,” Kore-eda Hirokazu’s “Look Back” and Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” feature Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” and Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson’s “Wicker” will receive their Canadian premieres, alongside Markus Schleinzer‘s “Rose.” 



	

					‘Rose’
									Courtesy of VIFF
	



	Other notable titles include Pedro Almodóvar’s “Bitter Christmas,” Peter Farrelly’s underdog story “I Play Rocky,” and Jordan Firstman’s Cannes breakout “Club Kid,” about an underground party promoter who discovers he has a kid—a role Firstman also plays. 

	This year’s selections, according to VIFF Director of Programming Curtis Woloschuk, lean into the anxiety of the moment. “In a lot of cases you see works talking about a humanist response to that,” he tells Variety. “Our duties of care within a family, within a community, within a city, and what forms that can take. That reverberates in both the narratives and the documentaries in the program.” 
	

	The theme, he says, arose organically while combing through submissions. He points to a cluster of films dealing with housing and economic uncertainty as well as gentrification: Clio Barnard’s “I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning,” John Wilson’s “The History of Concrete,” Noah Segan’s “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” and the Austrian entry “The Loneliest Man in Town.” 

	Several films are told from the perspective of the labor class, such as Radu Jude’s “Diary of a Chambermaid” and Xu Zao’s “Light Pillar,” a Chinese animated film about a custodian at a largely abandoned movie studio who escapes into (live action) VR. Meanwhile, “I Understand Your Displeasure,” part of the festival’s New German Cinema section, follows immigrants working as janitors in Berlin. 

	That undercurrent is also felt, explains Woloschuk, when it comes to a trio of documentaries he refers to as the ‘unofficial triptych of Canadian icons’: “Run Terry Run,” on Terry Fox’s legacy, Adrian Buitenhuis’s “Man in Motion: The Rick Hansen Story,” and Matthew Rankin’s “Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney.” Woloschuk points to present-day tariff disputes and debates over Canadian identity: “Sometimes another wrinkle in the headlines can suddenly take on greater significance.”  

	With more than 50 nonfiction features, including world premieres from B.C. filmmakers Joella Cabalu (“First Comes Love: Nakabingwit”) and David Ehrenreich (“Relax, Open Your Eyes”), VIFF is positioning itself as Canada’s second-largest documentary festival.  



	

					“First Comes Love: Nakabingwit’
	



	Woloschuk links the documentary push to the broader media landscape. “We live in a time where we are watching ongoing attacks on journalism and on documentary funding in the States,” he says, citing cuts to the National Endowment for the Arts and Humanities. “[There’s] a lot of assault on the truth, making it a slippery concept. I do think nonfiction films have this urgency embedded in them… they speak to the world that we inhabit, but also speak with a great sense of purpose.” 

	The festival’s Institute for the Moving Image, established earlier this year, will run its VIFF Industry and Amp Music in Media Summit programs Oct. 3-8 under the theme “Uncertainty as a Creative Force” – a title its director Ana Belén Asfura says was chosen to capture not just political uncertainty but “profound” technological upheaval across the industry. “We wanted to explore uncertainty not only as a challenge, but as a catalyst for creativity,” Asfura notes. “It is often in moments when the path forward is unclear that the most original ideas emerge.” 
	

	For Asfura, the Institute’s core mission has been to address the gap in the local screen ecosystem by “ensuring that local creators, particularly those from equity-deserving communities, are not only participating in the industry as service providers, but are also supported as artists with stories of their own to tell.”

	To that end, the Institute has launched three new artist development programs: Animation, Documentary and Creative Business. “We’ve begun building a year-round community of creators, industry professionals and partners that extends beyond the festival itself,” she says.  

	This year, Asfura adds, the goal is deepening those international ties: “We’re creating a space where local talent can develop their craft while becoming part of a global network of artists, industry leaders and opportunities, ensuring that VIFF is not only celebrating cinema, but also helping shape its future.” 

	Woloschuk sees the idea of community as an answer to uncertainty as something that runs through the festival at large. “What we’ve tried to do as an organization is create a Venn diagram of community and industry that almost completely overlaps, and understand that these things aren’t separate at all,” he says. 

	“As people further their own professional aims, they can do it by galvanizing themselves as a community as well,” he adds. “By creating these spaces for dialogue, it allows everyone to share where they’re at, share their own findings, and hopefully plot a path forward that can help move the greater sector as well.” 

	For all of its premieres, the festival, critically, remains a place of gathering. That ethos extends especially well to VIFF Live, the festival’s growing live performance strand. Curator Jarrett Martineau, who also heads programming at the Chan Centre, builds each show around “the intersection of the moving image and live music,” explains Woloschuk. This year’s edition includes the North American premiere of Jóhann Jóhannsson’s Cinematic Suites, performed with a full orchestra at the Chan Centre and drawing on his scores for Denis Villeneuve’s “Prisoners”, “Sicario” and “Arrival,” a reimagining David Lynch’s “Eraserhead” by experimental rock act Xiu Xiu, and An Evening with Mark Mothersbaugh, in which the DEVO frontman and prolific film composer performs selections from his scores, including work from “The Royal Tenenbaums,” “Rushmore,” “The LEGO Movie,” and “Thor: Ragnarok,” backed by a 16-piece ensemble. 
	

	Indigenous storytelling also features throughout this year’s program, anchored by Northern Lights, VIFF’s dedicated showcase for emerging Canadian and Indigenous filmmakers, with films by Nyla Innuksuk (“In the Heart of the South”), Alexandara Lzarowich (“Turtle Island Rap”), Cody Lightning’s “Smudge the Blades,” and Métis/Dene director Marie Clements, who brings both “How We Stand” and the world premiere of her Knowledge Network series “Reclaim My Skin.” Other films include “In the Heart of the South.” 

	The presence is felt at VIFF Live as well, with “Takkuk,” a film co-created with Indigenous artists across Greenland and Sápmi, preceded by live performances from Inuit throat-singing duo Silla and Greenlandic rapper Tarrak.



	

					Kyle Fostner, VIFF executive director; Ana Belén Asfura, director of the Institute for the Moving Image; Curtis Woloschuk, director of programming
									Courtesy of VIFF

title: WNBA Names Catbird Official Jewelry Partner, Launches Limited-Edition Basketball Collection
description:

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Catbird is bringing some Brooklyn sparkle to the WNBA.

	The New York-based jewelry brand has been named the WNBA’s official jewelry partner, becoming the league’s first-ever demi-fine jewelry partner. To mark the deal — and the WNBA’s milestone 30th season — the two are launching a limited-edition jewelry collection on Sept. 1.

	The Catbird x WNBA collection comprises three collectible charms inspired by the league’s history, players and hometown fandom. The Jumpwoman Charm recreates the silhouette from the WNBA’s official logo and is engraved with a commemorative 30th-season mark, while an Engravable Basketball Charm can be customized as a keepsake. A City Letter Charm, meanwhile, incorporates official WNBA team tricodes representing eight cities. Pieces are available in sterling silver and 10-karat solid gold, with prices starting at $74.


		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

										LIMITED-EDITION						

					WNBA x Catbird		

		
	

	The partnership arrives as the WNBA spends 2026 celebrating three decades since its founding. The league was approved by the NBA Board of Governors in April 1996 before beginning play in June 1997, and its 30th-season programming this year has included archival campaigns, merchandise drops, “Court Origins” nights and a countdown of the 30 greatest plays in league history.

	New York Liberty founding players Teresa Weatherspoon and Sue Wicks star in the campaign imagery. The partnership also continues Catbird’s push beyond traditional jewelry releases into entertainment, and pop-culture collaborations. In recent years, Catbird has worked with a wide-ranging roster of cultural names and institutions including Phoebe Bridgers, Boygenius, Clairo, Laufey, Japanese Breakfast, Jenny Slate and Amazon’s “The Summer I Turned Pretty.”


	Shop Catbird’s limited-edition WNBA collection here.

title: Jay Baruchel Is ‘The Stunt Driver’ in New Stills as IFC Comedy-Drama Heads to World Premiere at Toronto
description: The Independent Film Company has unveiled new stills from ”The Stunt Driver,“ which is making its world premiere at the Toronto Intl. Film Festival
body:
The Independent Film Company has unveiled new stills from ”The Stunt Driver,“ which is making its world premiere at the Toronto Intl. Film Festival Sept. 11. The Independent Film Company, which acquired the film July 21, will release the comedy-drama Sept. 25 theatrically.

	“The Stunt Driver,“ set in the mid-1970s, recounts the story of Canada’s Ken Carter, the world champion stunt driver who battles personal demons (and struggles under the long shadow of the more famous American stunt performer Evel Knievel) and public doubt to attempt what everyone considers impossible — a mile-long jump across the St. Lawrence River in a rocket car.
	

	Michael Dowse  directed and penned the screenplay. Jay Baruchel plays Carter, with Laurence Leboeuf as his steadfastly loving wife, Gloria. Ed Helms tackles the role of technician Dick Keller, who Carter enlists to design and build the rocket car. They end up in a poignant friendship over the years it takes to develop the car and plan the daring jump. Dan Bakkedahl also stars while Ben Foster makes an appearance as Knievel — Carter’s nemesis, or so he imagines.


	Carter‘s daring exploits were first brought to the screen in Robert Fortier’s 1981 documentary ”The Devil at Your Heels,“ the making of which is a key part of Dowse’s film. 

	Dowse and Baruchel brought the hit ice hockey feature ”Goon“ to TIFF in 2011.

	The film is produced by Jennifer Wilson and Michael Dowse for Film Cardinal, and executive produced by Baruchel, Joe Iacono, Dave Bishop and James Pugh for Protagonist Pictures, Lisa Wolofsky, Andrew Frank for Mongrel Media, and Cameron MacLaren.

title: Benedict Cumberbatch-Narrated Doc ‘How to Live on Earth’ Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “How to Live on Earth,” a feature documentary from Open Planet Studios and narrated by Benedict Cumberbatch, is set to premiere Sept. 20 on YouTube.
body:
“How to Live on Earth,” a feature documentary from Open Planet Studios and narrated by Benedict Cumberbatch, is set to premiere Sept. 20 on YouTube.

	Presented from London’s Natural History Museum, the film consists of segments from different contributors focusing on how humans can work with nature to build a safe and thriving future.

	Main contributors on the film include climate justice activist Xiye Bastida; field biologist, wildlife filmmaker and explorer Dan O’Neill; and former White House chef and senior policy advisor on nutrition Sam Kass.
	

	“We created ‘How to Live on Earth’ to be a catalyst for a much bigger conversation about our relationship with the natural world,” said Jonnie Hughes, executive producer and co-founder of Open Planet. “We’ve seen a growing appetite for hopeful stories that give people optimism and agency, and the global premiere on YouTube is a chance to turn that momentum into a truly shared moment.”


	The film’s premiere on YouTube is accompanied by the debut of “Chapter 4,” an original end credit track written, produced and performed by Imogen Heap.

	“How to Live on Earth” made its world premiere on June 22 at London’s Odeon Luxe Leicester Square and UK theatrical release on June 26. Ahead of the YouTube release, the film is making a series of regional premieres and screenings in Switzerland, Australia, Ecuador, the Netherlands, Hong Kong, Singapore, New Zealand and the United States.

	On Sept. 20, a special screening and Q&A of the documentary will kick off New York Climate Week at the Climate Film Festival in New York.
	

	The film’s release will be supported by a global impact campaign in partnership with a network of NGOs, UN Agencies and educational institutions.

	Watch the trailer for “How to Live on Earth” below.

schema.headline: Benedict Cumberbatch-Narrated Doc ‘How to Live on Earth’ Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE)

title: See Gracie Abrams Give an Intimate Performance of ‘Broke My Heart’ on Amazon Music’s ‘Songline’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Amazon Music has partnered with Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Gracie Abrams for a new episode of its docu-performance series “Songline” — and V
body:
Amazon Music has partnered with Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Gracie Abrams for a new episode of its docu-performance series “Songline” — and Variety has an exclusive preview of the song “Broke My Heart.”

	In the episode, recorded at the historic Church Studios in North London, Abrams revisits songs from her recent hit album, “Daughter from Hell,” through performances and candid conversations with longtime collaborator Aaron Dessner about the stories behind the music and their six-year creative partnership. The full “Songline” docu-performance film premieres on September 10.
	



	 “Songline” is a series dedicated to the craft of songwriting and invites artists to reimagine their music in a stripped-down, intimate setting. Each performance is intercut with in-depth interviews with the artist, giving fans a look behind the songwriting process. Recent “Songline” episodes have included Billie Eilish, Laufey, A$AP Rocky, Maren Morris, Reneé Rapp, Ed Sheeran, and more.


	“‘Songline’ gave me the chance to sit with these songs in a completely different way,” Abrams says. “When you strip everything back, you remember why you wrote them in the first place. It was really just me and my band in a room together, letting the songs breathe. There’s something scary and beautiful about that kind of intimacy.”

	Dessner adds, “It’s incredibly real and vulnerable and authentic — there’s nothing contrived about it. It’s the humanity in her writing. She gives voice to things. It’s very cathartic for people to listen to, and I think it’s why she’s connected so much with her fans, because it’s so personal and so intimate. The best work we’ve done is pushing ourselves to be more ambitious and go deeper.”

schema.headline: See Gracie Abrams Give an Intimate Performance of ‘Broke My Heart’ on Amazon Music’s ‘Songline’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: CBS News’ Abdul El-Sayed Post Sparks Digital Backlash
description: A CBS News headline accompanying a story about Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has generated significant online scrutiny, and th
body:
A CBS News headline accompanying a story about Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has generated significant online scrutiny, and the Paramount Skydance news outlet, once known for its reserve, appears to feel the facts presented in the work outweigh the digital opprobrium.

	On Monday morning, the CBS News feed on X posted a story with the accompanying headline: “As the nation prepares to mark 25 years since Sept. 11, 2001,” the post said, “Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, may be facing the risk of renewed scrutiny and fresh political attack.” The story described the candidate as someone who “opposed American wars and capitalized on anger over anti-Arab sentiment in a state with a robust and active Muslim community.” As evidence, the story cited two deleted posts that had originally surfaced in 2020 and compared the death toll from the coronavirus pandemic with the death toll from terrorist attacks on the U.S. on September 11, 2001.
	

	The post drew rebukes from a host of digital personalities and critics, including Cenk Uygur, host of “The Young Turks” and Tim Miller of The Bulwark.


	“Ma’am, hate to bother you, but I just wanted to let you know, your mask slipped off,” Uygur posted.  Miller called the CBS News post “despicable anti-Muslim woke right garbage.

	CBS News declined to make executives available for comment.

	A person familiar with the story said CBS News saw nothing wrong in reporting on a politician’s deleted tweets. This person also says CBS News interviewed El-Sayed later in the day Monday and added his response to the matter. The story also included comments from a Michigan State political scientist about whether the tweets might affect the race in Michigan . 

	The digital outrage bubbles as media critics and even journalists within CBS News scrutinize the decisions of Bari Weiss, installed by Paramount as editor in chief of CBS News in 2025, for bias or the insertion of opinion into the CBS News daily report. Weiss, founder of the online opinion site the Free Press, is known for railing against so-called “woke” extremes and for unwavering support of Israel. In the recent past, CBS News has been watched for the way it covers New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
	

	The media newsletter Status on Monday night reported that Weiss praised the story during the network’s daily editorial meeting Monday, and directed that the headline mention El-Sayed had deleted tweets referencing the September 11 terrorist attacks.

	But the person familiar with the CBS News article indicated Weiss sought a mention of the politician’s deleted tweets in the headline, since their discovery was a central part of the story. This person said CBS News deems El-Sayed’s past comments on 9/11 newsworthy, along with his association with the provocateur Hasan Piker, and how they might affect voters’ perception of his candidacy.

schema.headline: CBS News’ Abdul El-Sayed Post Sparks Digital Backlash

title: Variety Power of Women: Los Angeles Event Presented by Lifetime Announces Honorees Jennifer Hudson, Pearlena Igbokwe, Melissa McCarthy, Sharon Stone
description: Variety is pleased to announce the honorees for their upcoming Power of Women issue on Thursday, Sept. 17, with the event the following Wednesday. S
body:
Variety is pleased to announce the honorees for their upcoming Power of Women issue on Thursday, Sept. 17, with the event the following Wednesday. Sept. 23 in Beverly Hills. The event, in partnership with Lifetime, celebrates the Power of Women honorees, who will each appear on the cover of the issue, as well as the accomplished women profiled in the annual Women’s Impact Report, which highlights leaders in the entertainment industry.

	This year’s Power of Women honorees include Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony Award-winning artist Jennifer Hudson, whose powerhouse vocals and commanding performances have made her one of the entertainment industry’s most celebrated talents. As she gears up for the Sept. 14 premiere of the fifth season of 18-time Emmy-nominated “The Jennifer Hudson Show,” she is supporting the Jennifer Hudson Foundation. Honoree Pearlena Igbokwe has spent more than 35 years helping shape the medium of television across prestige cable, broadcast, studios, and now streaming, earning a reputation as one of its most influential leaders through her ability to identify culture-defining stories, champion talent, and advance a more inclusive industry. She is supporting A Better Chance. Emmy Award-winning and Academy Award-nominated actress, producer, and writer Melissa McCarthy also made this year’s Power of Women list. Her acclaimed work across television, blockbuster comedies and dramatic films has established her as one of Hollywood’s most versatile performers and she will next star in Netflix’s upcoming “The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey.” She is supporting the Joyful Heart Foundation. The final honoree is Academy Award-nominated, Emmy and Golden Globe-winning actress, producer, and recipient of the Nobel Peace Summit Award for her global activism, Sharon Stone, who was most recently seen in HBO’s final season of “Euphoria,” has spent more than four decades portraying complex and unforgettable characters, challenging industry expectations and cementing her status as one of the world’s most influential actors. She is supporting the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU).
	

	Variety will also honor TV personality, bestselling author and podcast host Paige DeSorbo with the Variety Courage Award, presented by Purina, which recognizes her powerful advocacy for survivors of abuse. In 2024, DeSorbo opened up on her podcast about surviving an abusive relationship at 19 — an experience she’d kept private for over a decade — and has since used her platform to remind others they are not alone. Through her relationship with her cat, Daphne, DeSorbo illustrates the powerful role pets can play in helping survivors feel safe, supported and loved. The recognition ties closely to the Purple Leash Project, a partnership with Purina and nonprofit RedRover that works together to support domestic violence survivors on both ends of the leash by helping create more safe spaces for survivors and their pets. Nearly half (48%) of domestic abuse survivors delay leaving abuse because they cannot take their pet with them, yet only 20% of domestic violence shelters nationwide currently accept pets. Together, Purina and RedRover are working toward providing one million safe nights for domestic abuse survivors and their pets by the end of 2030, to make sure they can stay together and heal together. Since 2019, they have awarded more than $2 million in grants to advance pet-friendly shelter access, so survivors don’t have to choose between their safety and the pets they love.
	

	The event will be hosted by actress, comedian, writer and author Iliza Shlesinger, who stars in the film “Chasing Summer,” which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.

	“As the founding presenting partner of Variety‘s Power of Women, we’re honored to join Variety once again in celebrating the extraordinary women shaping our industry, the impact they make both on and off screen, and the causes closest to their hearts,” said Paul Buccieri, President & Chairman, A+E Global Media. “Lifetime has spent more than four decades championing women and their stories, and this year’s honorees reflect that spirit. They each embody the courage and purpose that define true leadership.”

	“Variety Power of Women is one of our most meaningful celebrations, honoring the extraordinary women who are using their voices, creativity and influence to create meaningful change,” said Variety Co-President and Publisher Dea Lawrence. “We are proud to recognize this remarkable group of women and to continue our valued partnership with Lifetime in elevating their stories and amplifying their impact. This year’s honorees embody the courage, vision and determination it takes to challenge convention, open doors and create new opportunities for women. Their leadership is not only shaping our industry today — it is empowering the next generation of storytellers, innovators and leaders to see what is possible and know they have a place at the table.”

	Lifetime is the Presenting Partner of the event, and Purina is the Premier Partner of the event. Waymo, the leading autonomous vehicle technology company, is the Official Innovation Partner.

	Exclusive, curated gift bags will be given to honorees and guests at the event with entertainment, beauty, health and fashion products, from companies including BÉIS, YISE Beauty, Goop, Voluspa, Milk Makeup, OSEA, Tarte Cosmetics, ILIA and more.

schema.headline: Variety Power of Women: Los Angeles Event Presented by Lifetime Announces Honorees Jennifer Hudson, Pearlena Igbokwe, Melissa McCarthy, Sharon Stone

title: Brazil’s Globo, Turkey’s Ay Yapim Renew Alliance With Three-Format Deal, Readying Turkish Version of Brazil’s ‘Looks & Essence’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Globo, Latin America’s biggest media company, and Turkish telenovela powerhouse Ay Yapim, have renewed their alliance with a fresh three-title deal,
body:
Globo, Latin America’s biggest media company, and Turkish telenovela powerhouse Ay Yapim, have renewed their alliance with a fresh three-title deal, including a new Globo format adaptation by Ay Yapim, “Ömür Usta,” set to bow on Turkey’s Now free-to-air channel in September.

	The new multi-title partnership rolls off the Ay Yapim produced “Leyla,” the first international adaptation of Globo megahit “Brazil Avenue,” which has been sold by Madd Entertainment to over 100 countries.
	

	A longtime Ay Yapim creative who helmed many of its major hits such as “Fatmagül,” “Forbidden Love,” “Endless Love” (“Kara Sevda”) and indeed “Leyla,” Hilal Siral is directing “Ömür Usta,” adapting Globo hit telenovela “Looks & Essence” (“Fina Estampa”).


	From veteran Aguinaldo Silva (“Tieta,” “Anything Goes,” “Her Own Destiny”), one of Brazil’s great telenovela writers, who scored a recent ratings home-run in Brazil with “Three Graces,” 2011 Globo telenovela “Looks & Essence” turned on Griselda (Lília Cabral), an honorable hardworking humble handywoman who still performs household repairs in her fancy neighborhood. “‘Looks & Essence’ explores the contrast between appearance and character, questioning what truly holds value in contemporary society,” Globo said in a statement Tuesday.

	Telemundo produced a Spanish-language reversion “Marido en Alquiler” in 2013. Madd Entertainment will handle international distribution on all three new Ay Yapim Globo adaptations.  In Brazil, the new adaptations may also become available across Globo’s platforms, including Globoplay and Globoplay Novelas TV channel, Globo said Tuesday.
	

	“This partnership reinforces the global appeal of Brazilian storytelling,” said Globo head of international business Angela Colla. “Working with Ay Yapım demonstrates how open we are to new business models and creative collaborations. The success of ‘Leyla’ reflects the universal nature of our narratives, and we are excited to see more Globo stories come to life in other cultures.”

	First unveiled at Mipcom 2023 as part of Madd Entertainment’s first five year’s anniversary, the Globo-Ay Yapim partnership builds on the dramatic expansion of Turkish telenovelas into Latin America and more latterly Europe, led by Spain and Italy, where Madd Entertainment sealed a four-title sale to Mediaset in 2024.

	One of Latin America’s companies which has stood up most energetically to competition from global streamers, Globo has diversified fast its business models from the last decade, initiating format sales and distribution, partnering with MFF & Co on an English-language multiple-season series slate reversioning its hit telenovelas, while driving into co-production with a welter of top international players unveiled at last year’s Mipcom, such as Ron Leshem, BBC, Fox Entertainment Studios, Beta Film and Gaumont USA.

	Via its enterprising SVOD arm Globoplay, Globo has also driven into stylish upscale series whose ambitions can make them stand out from the crowd, such as “Emergency 53,” which won the coveted Studio Babelsberg Production Excellence Award at the 2026 Berlinale Series Market, competing with shows from around the world.

schema.headline: Brazil’s Globo, Turkey’s Ay Yapim Renew Alliance With Three-Format Deal, Readying Turkish Version of Brazil’s ‘Looks & Essence’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Spike Jonze Launches Limited-Edition Eyewear Collection With Warby Parker
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Spike Jon
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Spike Jonze is putting his director’s eye on a different kind of frame.

	The Oscar-winning filmmaker has teamed with Warby Parker on a limited-edition eyewear collection launching Sept. 1, reviving four of his favorite discontinued frames from the brand’s archives. Jonze has worn Warby Parker glasses for more than a decade and is a regular at the company’s Glendale, Calif., store. Last year, he approached the brand himself about collaborating, eventually landing on the idea of bringing back several sold-out styles he still wears.



						
			
	

	
					

	The resulting lineup includes four optical and sunglass styles, with prices starting at $95: the Percey in Rose Crystal with Riesling, originally released in September 2018; Begley in Magnolia Green, first released in November 2020; Locke in Layered Cacao Crystal, a December 2021 style; and Yoojin in Brioche Tortoise with Riesling, which debuted in December 2022.

	Jonze offers his own “director’s commentary” on each pair. Of the pink Percey frames, he recalls having lost several other versions before learning at the Glendale store that his surviving pair was rare. He gravitated toward Begley for its flat-top rim, while Locke appealed to him for a recessed lower rim and narrow arms that he says evoke “an Italian actor of the 1960s.” Yoojin, meanwhile, stood out because putting them on made him feel “so sophisticated,” like he had discovered “a little gem.”

	Each pair arrives with a letter from the director and fluorescent heavy-duty stickers inspired by the handwritten gaffer’s-tape labels he uses to organize his own ever-expanding Warby Parker collection.


	For the campaign, Opening Ceremony co-founder Humberto Leon photographed five people from Jonze’s orbit — skater and artist Jerry Hsu, model Jane Moseley, filmmakers Skylar-Bree Takyi and Henry Zumbrunnen and Leon’s mother, Wendy — wearing the revived frames along with actual clothes pulled from Jonze’s closet.

	Leon’s involvement also reconnects Jonze with one of his longest-running relationships in fashion. In 2009, Opening Ceremony released a collection tied to Jonze’s “Where the Wild Things Are,” translating the film’s creatures into faux-fur coats, vests and an adult-sized version of Max’s white hooded suit. The retailer later created a capsule inspired by the distinctive high-waisted trousers, color-blocked shirts and jackets of Jonze’s “Her.”

	The relationship became even more intertwined with Opening Ceremony’s runway presentations. Jonze and Jonah Hill wrote “100% Lost Cotton,” a one-act play that replaced the brand’s traditional Spring 2015 fashion show, with Jonze directing a cast that included Elle Fanning, Catherine Keener, Rashida Jones and Bobby Cannavale. For Opening Ceremony’s Fall 2015 menswear collection, Jonze opened his personal archive of skate, BMX and behind-the-scenes photography, which Leon and Carol Lim turned into clothing prints featuring everything from skaters to stills from the Beastie Boys’ “Sabotage” video. He later wrote and directed the brand’s 2017 theatrical presentation “Changers,” starring Lakeith Stanfield and Mia Wasikowska.

	More recently, Jonze has returned to fashion from behind the camera. Earlier this year, he wrote and directed “Shape of Dreams,” the surreal campaign film starring Zendaya for her first co-created apparel and footwear collection with On and stylist Law Roach. The project went on to win a Gold Lion and two Silver Lions at the 2026 Cannes Lions festival.

	Shop Jonze’s Warby Parker collection here.

title: See Hayden Panettiere's Boyfriend Brian Hickerson Hiding Under Table Before 2025 Arrest
description:
Hayden Panettiere's Boyfriend
                          Wild Photo Shows Him Hiding Under Table B
body:
Hayden Panettiere's Boyfriend
                          Wild Photo Shows Him Hiding Under Table Before L.A. Arrest
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                August 31, 2026
                
                            4:41 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 1, 2026
                                6:36 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere's boyfriend Brian Hickerson was seen barefoot and hunkered down under a restaurant table moments before his 2025 Los Angeles arrest ... and TMZ has obtained a photo from the bizarre scene.
      
    
            The pic was snapped August 2, 2025 inside Barney's Beanery in West Hollywood ... showing Brian sitting on the floor underneath a table with his shoes off as a Los Angeles County Sheriff's deputy stands nearby.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ ... Brian came into Barney's and appeared to be under the influence of something and acted erratically. Sources say he allegedly broke a drinking glass at the bar. We're told things escalated when Brian allegedly threw one of his shoes at another person who was eating inside the restaurant ... prompting staff to ask him to leave.
      

            Our sources say Brian started freaking out and an employee attempted to physically remove him ... but he refused to go, so cops were called. We're told law enforcement also had a difficult time getting Brian out of the restaurant ... but deputies eventually removed him and arrested him outside.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The owner of Barney's Beanery tells TMZ ... Brian was not permanently banned from the restaurant. He's allowed to return.
      
    
            Prosecutors declined to file charges due to insufficient evidence. He was arrested again four days later for allegedly being under the influence of a controlled substance, entered a diversion program and had the case dismissed after completing 10 Narcotics Anonymous meetings.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            TMZ also broke the story ... Brian was permanently banned from at least three South Carolina bars two to three months before Hayden's death, with sources telling us those bans stemmed from concerns over excessive drinking.
      
    
            As you know, Brian was with Hayden August 16th when she was found unresponsive. He used Narcan in an attempt to revive her, to no avail. Her death is currently under investigation.

title: Jared Leto Sells Massive L.A. Air Force Compound For $12 Million
description:
Jared Leto
                          At Ease Soldiers, I Sold My L.A. Air Force Compound!!!
body:
Jared Leto
                          At Ease Soldiers, I Sold My L.A. Air Force Compound!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 1, 2026
                            7:31 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jared Leto has quietly offloaded his massive L.A. mansion -- a former Air Force compound -- and the timing of the sale might raise some eyebrows.
      
    
            We've learned the actor and singer sold his 14,649-square-foot mansion in May for $12 million ... a tidy profit after buying the pad for $5 million back in 2015.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The 6-bedroom, 5-bathroom home -- which sits on a 1.4-acre lot -- has a colorful history ... having previously been a U.S. Air Force installation with connections to the country's atomic bomb program.
      
    
            Army training films and Air Force newsreels were also shot at the property during the Cold War ... and the short reels even featured huge stars like Bob Hope, Jimmy Stewart, James Garner, Kim Novak and Gregory Peck.
      
    
            The main structure has 3 35-millimeter screening rooms and temperature-controlled film vaults. It also has a full sound stage.
      
    
            Leto's decision to let the place go comes during a particularly turbulent time in the star's life ... with the house selling just two months before the BBC released its documentary in which multiple women accused Leto of sexual assault. Several allegations against him first cropped up in British newspapers last year.
      
    
            While he's vigorously denied all wrongdoing, he's receded from the spotlight in recent months ... and making the quiet decision to leave Los Angeles seems to indicate he's done with Hollywood in the long term.

title: Lindsay Clancy Jurors Deadlocked, Judge Orders Them to Press On
description:
Lindsay Clancy Jury
                          We're Deadlocked
                          ... Judg
body:
Lindsay Clancy Jury
                          We're Deadlocked
                          ... Judge Says Keep Trying
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 1, 2026
                            7:44 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder case told the Judge Tuesday morning that they can't reach a unanimous verdict on any of the counts, but the judge isn't ready to throw in the towel.
      
    
            The jurors deliberated for 18 hours before they threw their hands up in the air. Jurors are trying to decide if Clancy is guilty of murder, manslaughter, or not guilty by lack of criminal responsibility. The lack of criminal responsibility is essentially an insanity defense.
      
    
            It's clear some of the jurors were entertaining the lack of criminal responsibility defense when they asked to see the knife she allegedly used to slash herself and the pill bottles.
      
    
            The jury has gone back to deliberate.
      
    
            As we previously reported ... Clancy’s defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, has argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis when her three children -- Cora, Dawson and Callan -- died at the family's Massachusetts home in January 2023.
      
    
            Prosecutors maintain Lindsay was criminally responsible.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Lindsay has pleaded not guilty ... however, she acknowledges killing the children. Her ex-husband Patrick Clancy has already taken the witness stand, describing the devastating discovery of his children and his call to 911 which was played in court.
      
    
            Now, by order of the judge, Lindsay's fate still remains in the hands of the jury ... if they can ever come to an unanimous agreement.

D4vd
                          Family Sold Off Texas Home, Took Out $138K Loan
                          As Singer Struggled to Pay Legal Team
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 1, 2026
                            8:30 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            D4vd’s father was making interesting financial moves in the past couple of months ... while his son faced money issues and is now repped by a public defender in his murder case ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            TMZ obtained real estate records showing D4vd’s dad, Dawud Burke, sold a 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom, 1,819-square-foot home in Houston, Texas, for $229,000 in early July.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A couple months earlier in late April, documents show Dawud took out a $138K loan on a different property in Houston ... which appears to be a 3-bedroom, 1-bathroom, 1,260-square-foot home.
      

            Dawud currently lives in a 4-bedroom, 3-bathroom, 4,426-square-foot home in Hempstead, Texas, with an estimated value of $850K.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            D4vd’s dad selling a huge asset comes as the singer was declared indigent, leading to the withdrawal of his powerhouse legal team, consisting of Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski, and Regina Peter. He will now be represented by a public defender in his criminal case over Celeste Rivas' murder.
      
    
            The singer being without funds to pay his legal team is noteworthy given the $11 million he made from his Interscope deal alone.
